source.title: Deep Learning to Predict Late-Onset Breast Cancer Metastasis: the Single Hyperparameter Grid Search (SHGS) Strategy for Meta Tuning Concerning Deep Feed-forward Neural Network
source.authors: Yi-Jun Zhou; Om Arora-Jain; Xia Jiang

record.tranche_reason: Sweeps batch size and dropout and reports their association with held-out test AUC; these are conceptual tests of parts of V5 and V6, using clinical prediction datasets and AUC rather than the claim versions’ stated settings.
record.gate_note: The study varies eight hyperparameters, but optimizer-specific outcomes are not reported; optimizer is randomly selected among background settings. Results about epochs, L1, L2, learning rate, momentum, decay, and running time do not test the listed versions. Figure-level experiment values are not reconstructed beyond the explicitly stated dataset-level best scores and trends.
record.test_reason: Batch-size and dropout sweeps measure held-out discrimination in fully connected clinical classifiers, extending parts of V5 and V6 to a new setting. Within each sweep, other hyperparameters, including epochs, are fixed; their values differ across the ten background settings.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: optimal hyperparameters depend on the dataset and other hyperparameters, and SHGS can help select reduced ranges for low-budget grid search. The authors also explicitly conclude that both low and high batch sizes can yield optimal models under different background settings.
record.recipe_differences: Clinical DFNN hyperparameter sweeps using SHGS, five-fold cross-validation, and independent test AUC; not the claim versions’ stated architectures, tasks, or comparison recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that outcomes can differ across randomly selected background hyperparameter settings and datasets.
record.problems: The figures are the main source of per-setting outcomes; the text gives qualitative summaries and dataset-level best scores but not the individual numeric comparisons. Background settings vary randomly, and no direct fixed-epoch-budget comparison is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately reported numeric batch-size or dropout values are available in the text. Figure panels contain ten scatter plots per dataset and hyperparameter, but individual coordinates are figure-only and are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Optimizer-specific held-out comparisons under defined tuning budgets.
Image and language workloads; recovery through longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization or regularization changes. No quantitative workload-dependent threshold is established.

Improvement over no dropout cannot be established from the supplied textual summaries. Convolutional classifiers, training-set-size dependence, underfitting as the mechanism, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation are not established.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and correlations with generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable plotted coordinates. Per-setting numeric results are already declared omitted in rows_left_out. AUC measures discrimination rather than classification error, and selected maximum AUCs do not quantify intervention effects. Neither sharp minimizers nor dropout-induced underfitting was measured.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Network width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization; optimizer settings were not reported by outcome.
Image-classification and language benchmarks, large batches beyond workload-dependent size, and comparisons under fixed epoch budgets with adapted recipes.
Fully connected and convolutional classifiers, very small training sets, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Removal of memorized training examples and resulting test accuracy.
